summary: GetLastError on a thread returns exactly the value the thread's most recent SetLastError call was given, when no call between them sets the last-error code.
applicability: Windows desktop, kernel32 (Windows XP and later per the pages cited)

execution.main: QueryPerformanceCounter once, before any SetLastError; three values chosen from that count, consecutive values different; for each value v: SetLastError(v), then, with no intervening call that sets the last-error code, GetLastError()

evidence.quote: Sets the last-error code for the calling thread. ... The last-error code is kept in thread local storage so that multiple threads do not overwrite each other's values.

The return value is the calling thread's last-error code. ... If the function is not documented to set the last-error code, the value returned by this function is simply the most recent last-error code to have been set

open_questions: The values come from a 256-entry table built into the probe (probes/last_error_values/values.h), so the trace can carry true args_sha256 values without hashing in the guest; a candidate that ignores its argument passes one pair with probability 1/256 at most, and consecutive pairs use different values.
QueryPerformanceCounter is used only to choose values; its own behavior is not judged here (v0.2 section 3.1 gives clocks their own contracts).

sections.supersedes: 0.1.0, whose one fixed value (SetLastError(1234)) let a candidate returning the constant 1234 conform (Sprint 031).
